version: v5.0 (Nov 19 2026): Codex's moving demos, start-to-finish pictures, ride timer and wind plan, and readiness check, merged into v4.2.

core.name: Morning sunlight
core.dose: 5–10 min outside within an hour of waking; 15–20 if cloudy
core.built: Ride days: done by riding outside. Lift days: the cool-down walk is outside.
core.why: Light in the eyes early sets the body clock, which drives sleep quality, morning alertness and evening melatonin.

core.name: Sleep 7–9 hours, same wake time
core.dose: Dark, cool room; last caffeine 8–10 h before bed; no alcohol close to bed
core.who: Huberman · Peter Attia · Matthew Walker · ACSM
core.built: Your 6:00 wake-up is already fixed. Your watch tracks the rest.
core.why: Sleep is when muscle repairs and memory consolidates; short sleep raises the risk of nearly every chronic disease.

core.name: Easy cardio (Zone 2), 150+ min a week
core.dose: Talking pace, most of your cardio
core.who: Peter Attia · Huberman · WHO and ACSM guidelines
core.built: Monday and Wednesday rides, plus walks.
core.why: Most endurance training in successful programs is easy (about 80%), with a small hard dose (Seiler's polarized-training research).

core.name: One hard cardio session a week
core.who: Peter Attia · Huberman · Helgerud et al.
core.why: Cardio fitness was one of the strongest predictors of long life in 120,000 treadmill tests (Mandsager et al., JAMA Netw Open, 2018).

core.name: Strength training 2+ days a week
core.dose: All major muscles, near failure, getting heavier over time
core.who: Peter Attia · Jeff Nippard · ATHLEAN-X · ACSM
core.built: Lift A Tuesday, Lift B Thursday, optional Lift C Saturday.
core.why: Muscle and strength protect blood sugar, bones and independence; strength falls fastest after 50 unless trained.

core.name: Enough protein
core.dose: About 1.6 g per kg of body weight a day, spread over meals
core.why: Protein above about 1.6 g per kg of body weight a day adds little more muscle (Morton et al., BJSM, 2018).

core.name: Move all day
core.dose: 7,000–8,000 steps; a 10-min walk after the biggest meal
core.built: Not yet tracked. Duet can add steps from your watch later.
core.why: Health benefits of daily steps level off around 7,000–8,000 (Paluch et al., Lancet Public Health, 2022).

core.name: Balance and stability
core.dose: 1–2 min a day on one leg; get up off the floor without hands
core.who: Peter Attia · Knees Over Toes · Movement by David
core.built: In every lift-day cool-down and the daily stretch.
core.why: Not being able to stand 10 seconds on one leg in mid-life was linked to higher death risk (Araújo et al., BJSM, 2022). The sit-to-rise test (getting up off the floor) tracked with survival (Brito et al., Eur J Prev Cardiol, 2012).

core.name: Grip and carries
core.dose: Dead hang toward 2 min total; heavy carries
core.built: Farmer and suitcase carries; hangs in the warm-up and cool-down.
core.why: Low grip strength predicted earlier death across 17 countries (Leong et al., Lancet, 2015).

core.name: Daily mobility
core.dose: 10 min: hips, hamstrings, ankles, upper back, shoulders
core.who: Knees Over Toes · JR Stretch · Movement by David · CaliMove
core.why: Range of motion is use-it-or-lose-it. All four movement coaches agree on the same short list: hips, ankles, hamstrings, upper back and shoulders.

core.name: Calm the stress response
core.dose: 1–5 min of physiological sighs, or a short meditation
core.built: Every cool-down ends with sighs; a meditation link each day.
core.why: 5 min a day of cyclic sighing improved mood more than mindfulness meditation in a month-long trial (Balban et al., Cell Rep Med, 2023).

core.name: Little or no alcohol, no smoking
core.why: Both are among the clearest, best-documented drags on healthy lifespan and on sleep.

core.name: Yearly check-up and blood work
core.why: Blood pressure, cholesterol (including ApoB), blood sugar (A1c) and vitamin D catch problems early and guide supplements.

stretch.name: Couch stretch
stretch.cue: Back knee on a cushion against the couch, squeeze that glute, stay tall. Opens the hip flexors that sitting shortens.
stretch.home: Against the couch or a wall.

stretch.name: Hamstring rocks
stretch.cue: Soft knees, hinge at the hips, rock gently into the back of the leg.

stretch.name: 90/90 hip switches
stretch.cue: Both knees at 90°, rotate side to side, stay tall.

stretch.name: Knee-to-wall ankle stretch
stretch.cue: Foot a hand's width from the wall, drive the knee toward the wall, heel down.

stretch.name: Deep squat hold
stretch.cue: Sink into the bottom of a squat, heels down if you can; hold the chair for support.

stretch.name: Open book
stretch.cue: Side-lying, open the top arm across, follow it with your eyes.

stretch.name: Chest opener
stretch.cue: Hold a broomstick or belt behind your shoulders and open the chest in an easy range.

video.title: Chest stretch with broomstick or belt

stretch.name: Dead hang or lat sink
stretch.cue: Relaxed hang from the bar. No bar: on all fours, sink your hips back with arms long.

stretch.name: Single-leg stand
stretch.cue: Tall on one foot; close your eyes when it's easy.
stretch.why: Not being able to stand 10 seconds on one leg in mid-life was linked to higher death risk (Araújo et al., BJSM, 2022).

green.label: Good to go
green.text: Slept all right, feel normal: do the card as written.

yellow.label: So-so
yellow.text: Poor sleep, unusual soreness or low energy: stop every set with 3 good reps left and drop one set from each lift. Ride days: easy pace only; swap the 4×4 for an easy ride.

red.label: Not today
red.text: Sick, dizzy, chest pressure, faintness or unusual breathlessness: no workout today. Rest, and get checked if it doesn't pass.

afterLastWeek: Repeats weeks 7–12 until the next block is published.
